integrations.name: Email provider
integrations.purpose: Two-way sync of sent/received email into the CRM timeline.

integrations.name: Calendar provider
integrations.purpose: Two-way sync of meetings between the CRM and an external calendar.

integrations.name: Telephony / VoIP
integrations.purpose: Place calls from a record (click-to-call) and log the call, its duration, and its recording back against the contact automatically.

provenance.notes: SuiteCRM models Calls as a first-class module (with Calls_Reschedule); Odoo ships voip as a separate addon. Both keep the call as a CRM record and the carrier as an integration, which is the shape recorded here. No standard governs call logging.

integrations.name: Web Forms and Lead Capture
integrations.purpose: Create a lead from a website form, landing page, or chat widget, with campaign attribution attached.
examples: an embedded form posting to a capture endpoint

provenance.notes: Three independent implementations: EspoCRM has LeadCapture and LeadCaptureLogRecord entityDefs in core; Odoo ships crm with UTM attribution (the `utm` model) and website form integration; SuiteCRM has Prospects/ProspectLists fed by campaign web-to-lead. Capture and attribution travel together in all three.

integrations.name: Marketing Email / Campaign Sending
integrations.purpose: Send a campaign to a segment through a bulk-sending provider, and feed opens, clicks, bounces, and unsubscribes back onto the contact.

provenance.notes: Three independent implementations: SuiteCRM has Campaigns with EmailMan as the send queue; Odoo has the mass_mailing addon; EspoCRM has Campaign plus TargetList with opt-out state. Bounce/unsubscribe feedback is what makes this an integration rather than plain SMTP.

integrations.name: Contact / Company Enrichment
integrations.purpose: Fill in firmographic or contact detail from an external data provider after a lead arrives with only an email or domain.

provenance.notes: Only one implementation verified: Odoo ships crm_iap_enrich as a separate paid-credit addon. Neither EspoCRM core nor SuiteCRM has an equivalent, so this is recorded as optional at low confidence rather than a common expectation.

integrations.name: Accounting / Invoicing
integrations.purpose: Hand a won deal or an accepted quote to the system that raises the invoice, and read payment status back onto the record.

provenance.notes: Two independent implementations: SuiteCRM converts AOS_Quotes into AOS_Invoices and AOS_Contracts in core; Odoo's sale addon carries account_move/account_move_line, wiring the order to the ledger. Where the boundary sits differs, which is why this is `recommended` rather than core.

integrations.name: Public API and Outbound Webhooks
integrations.purpose: Let other systems read and write CRM records, and notify them when a record changes, so the CRM is not the only place data can enter.
examples: a REST or GraphQL API with token auth

provenance.notes: Three independent implementations: EspoCRM exposes a REST API and Webhook entity; Twenty is GraphQL-first over its workspace entities; SuiteCRM ships a V8 REST API. Overlaps no shared capability — an API surface is part of what a CRM is expected to be.
